items.title_zh: Claude 解决黑洞物理学中的两个开放问题
items.summary: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in theoretical physics: it completed a 2003 calculation showing the Hawking-Page transition stays abrupt at weak coupling in N=4 super Yang-Mills, and found the optimal ceiling for the modular bootstrap in 3D gravity (about c/9.1266). items.title: Hy-MT3: More Accurate, Robust and Practical Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild
items.raw_content:
Authors: Mao Zheng, Zheng Li, Fangxu Liu, Tao Chen, Bingxin Qu et al.

Hy-MT3 is the third generation of the Hunyuan multilingual translation model family, including \textbf{Hy-MT3-1.8B}, \textbf{Hy-MT3-7B} and \textbf{Hy-MT3-30B-A3B (MoE)}. Compared with Hy-MT2, Hy-MT3 translates \textbf{more accurately, more completely and more faithfully to user constraints}: on real-world scenario data, the share of samples with mistranslations is reduced by \textbf{43\%}, omissions or additions by \textbf{74\%}, and instruction-following errors by \textbf{40\%}, while language coverage is expanded from \textbf{38 to 102} languages. With only 3B activated parameters, \textbf{Hy-MT3-30B-A3B achieves the best overall performance among all evaluated models in non-thinking mode}, including flagship models such as Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi-K3.1-Pro and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and approaches the strongest closed-source thinking models such as GPT-6.1-Sol and Gemini-4-Argon, while surpassing models that consume \textbf{more than 30$\times$} its inference compute. Beyond general translation, Hy-MT3 is optimized for two industrial scenarios. For \textbf{game localization}, built with high-quality game-domain data and a professional evaluation system from the Honor of Kings team, Hy-MT3-30B-A3B matches or outperforms strong closed-source models such as Gemini 3.1 Pro on all core metrics, and can be plugged into game development pipelines through an open-source toolchain. For \textbf{image translation}, Hy-MT3 improves context understanding and error correction to better tolerate OCR errors, achieving the best result among models of comparable size. Finally, we open-source \textbf{TransRubric}, a rubric-based automatic evaluation suite for translation, which outperforms other evaluation schemes on the WMT26 metrics shared task test set and is more stable with respect to human evaluation.
items.title_zh: Hy-MT3：更准确、更稳健的多语言翻译模型系列
items.summary: The third-generation Hunyuan multilingual translation family spans 1.8B, 7B and 30B-A3B MoE models, expands coverage from 38 to 102 languages, and cuts mistranslations by 43%, omissions or additions by 74% and instruction-following errors by 40% versus Hy-MT2 on real-world data; the 30B-A3B model with 3B active parameters is reported to lead evaluated models in non-thinking mode.

items.title: FOREST: Coordinating Tree-based HBF, RRAM, and HBM for Efficient Speculative LLM Inference
items.raw_content:
Authors: Hao Ding, Zheng Shi, Dongxue Zhao, Huiying Bian, Meng Li et al.

Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by combining lightweight drafting with parallel target-model verification. However, its stages impose distinct resource demands: target verification requires high-throughput access to large weight sets, sequential drafting executes a compact model under tight latency constraints, and long-context attention processes growing key-value (KV) caches. Conventional GPU-centric SD systems serve these workloads through shared HBM-centric memory and general-purpose compute, creating mismatches in capacity, bandwidth, and computation. These mismatches constrain deployable model-context configurations and limit the efficiency of bandwidth-bound and latency-sensitive operations.
  We propose FOREST, a heterogeneous memory-centric architecture coordinating HBF, 3D-stacked RRAM, and HBM memory-compute trees for efficient SD. It features: (1) compute-aligned 3D RRAM, combining ultra-wide, low-frequency reads with clock-decoupled interfaces and overlapped SRAM-DCIM weight refills for latency-sensitive drafting; (2) cross-tree numerical co-design, moving block-scaled Q/K/V preprocessing to HBF and RRAM root plates and enabling block-floating-point (BFP) attention with pipelined softmax reduction in the HBM tree; and (3) HBF-aware SD design-space exploration, revealing how bandwidth-compute provisioning and model scale determine performance, energy, and cost trade-offs. Evaluated across six SD configurations spanning 32B-405B target models, FOREST achieves up to 5.5x end-to-end speedup, 11.46x higher decode throughput, and 16.5x higher decode energy efficiency over NVIDIA A800 GPU-based SD baselines. Under a modeled total cost of ownership, FOREST delivers up to 6.73x higher token-generation cost efficiency.
items.title_zh: FOREST：协同 HBF、RRAM 与 HBM 的树状异构内存加速投机解码
items.summary: FOREST proposes a heterogeneous memory-centric architecture that coordinates HBF, 3D-stacked RRAM and HBM compute trees for speculative LLM decoding, reporting up to 5.5x end-to-end speedup, 11.46x higher decode throughput and 16.5x better decode energy efficiency than NVIDIA A800 GPU baselines across six configurations with 32B-405B target models.

items.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
items.raw_content:
Authors: Jingyi Zhou, Yi Liu, Bin Sun, Hongji Zhang, Dongsheng Zuo et al.

Large Language Models show great potential for automated Register-Transfer Level repair, yet they struggle with non-local faults where root causes and failing outputs reside far apart in source code. Treating RTL as a flat token sequence obscures hardware dataflows, whereas exposing complete synthesized graphs overwhelms the model with fine-grained metadata. To resolve this representation dilemma, we propose GRODE-RTL, an anchor-centric representation that extracts the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, maps netlist nodes back to editable source lines, and organizes them into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. By prioritizing direct drivers and folding distant hops, GRODE-RTL guides standard tool-using agents without exposing ground-truth hints or oracle feedback. We evaluate GRODE-RTL across 30 formally validated non-local faults using three LLMs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, and MiniMax-M3) alongside a controlled six-configuration ablation study. GRODE-RTL improves pass@1 over source-level exploration by 16.7% on DeepSeek, by 26.7% on GLM-5.2, and by 20.0% on MiniMax-M3, with consistent gains on the hard-to-retrieve far-distance and indirect-anchor subsets of all three models. Our controls isolate structural relevance from generic context expansion, proving that selective dependency organization rather than full graph exposure is key to effective RTL repair.
items.title_zh: GRODE-RTL：面向 LLM RTL 修复的源映射依赖视图
items.summary: GRODE-RTL represents suspect registers as compact, source-mapped dependency views for LLM-based RTL repair; it improves pass@1 by 16.7–26.7% across DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2 and MiniMax-M3.

items.title: HETEROVLM: Edge Multi-Request Vision-Language Model Serving on a Heterogeneous Versal SoC with AI Engines and Programmable Logic
items.raw_content:
Authors: Zhiheng Chen, Yu-An Chou, Yifan Zhang, Ye Qiao, Saptarshi Mitra et al.

Edge devices in vehicles and robots serve concurrent requests with different deadlines to a vision-language model (VLM), each mixing a compute-bound encoder and prefill with a memory-bound decode. GPU serving targets datacenter throughput with per-iteration host scheduling: an urgent request waits for the running iteration, and small-batch decode costs much energy per token. Prior accelerators on Versal AI Engine (AIE) SoCs map one model onto a fixed AIE dataflow graph for one input stream, without decode or request scheduling. HETEROVLM keeps the AIE graph static and makes it schedulable. The AIE array runs the encoder, prefill and attention, and the programmable logic (PL) holds GEMV engines for small decode steps and a scheduler that orders short work units by class and deadline. Concurrent requests share one decode step that reads the weights once. An urgent request preempts at a work-unit boundary, and the paused request resumes from its results in DDR. On an AMD Versal VC1902, text and camera questions get their first tokens in 140 and 303 ms. HETEROVLM decodes a single request 1.3x and 4.0x faster than NVIDIA Tesla T4 and Jetson Orin Nano GPUs, with 61% and 73% of their energy per token, and uses 51% of the energy per token of an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti. The same bitstream serves multiple VLMs by loading their own instruction programs and weights. A demo is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/demo heterovlm-EFM2/.
items.title_zh: HETEROVLM：在 Versal SoC 上服务边缘多请求 VLM
items.summary: HETEROVLM is an edge multi-request vision-language model serving system on a heterogeneous Versal SoC, using a static AI Engine graph for encoder, prefill and attention plus programmable-logic GEMV engines and a deadline-aware scheduler for small decode steps; concurrent requests share one decode step that reads weights once.

items.title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis
items.raw_content:
Authors: Minh Luu, Michael Quinn, Aakash Tyagi, David Houngninou, Jiang Hu

AI-assisted RTL localization and debugging need ground-truth bug datasets with known locations and observable failures, while testbench grading uses injected bugs to measure detection capability. Creating such datasets at scale remains a major EDA challenge. BugGen 1.0 shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate context-aware RTL mutations. Still, it relies on the model for both choosing where to mutate and generating the edit, which increases inference costs and can lead to invalid choices. BugGen 2.0 changes this division of labor. Deterministic algorithms handle structural analysis, target selection, and validation, while the LLM focuses on localized semantic rewriting. Across four OpenTitan IP blocks and FabScalar with three LLMs, BugGen 2.0 reaches every requested quota of compilable bug scenarios that cause at least two test failures, with 14-16 of 16 configured mutation types represented. In completed same-model comparisons, it reduces token use by 6.8x-15.4x relative to BugGen 1.0 and 1.5x-7.9x relative to Firefly. BugGen 2.0 also expands the dataset without simulating every new bug. After finding accepted scenarios with observable failures, it generates alternative mutations at the same locations, simulates only a subset, and estimates acceptance for the rest. This skips 63.6% of AES and 33.9% of FabScalar variant simulations. Full simulation finds that 77.7% of AES variants and 95.2% of FabScalar variants are accepted, with a 1.09% estimation error on the directly comparable FabScalar set. These results show that focusing LLMs on semantic rewriting lowers inference and simulation cost while improving consistency across models and designs.
items.title_zh: BugGen 2.0：重新划分 LLM 在可扩展 RTL Bug 合成中的角色
items.summary: BugGen 2.0 uses deterministic algorithms for structural analysis, target selection and validation while the LLM focuses on localized semantic rewriting; across four OpenTitan IP blocks, FabScalar and three LLMs, it reaches every requested quota of compilable bug scenarios causing at least two test failures, with 14–16 of 16 mutation types represented.

items.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
items.raw_content:
Authors: Haosong Peng, Xiangyang Liu, Zhengshen Zhang, Yunfeng Fan, Tianyu Qi et al.

Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states. Our new cross-embodiment augmentation pipeline converts existing RGB videos into demonstrations for alternative embodiments by retargeting the recovered motion and synthesizing the corresponding observations, without recorded source-robot states. Experiments show that the tracker achieves absolute trajectory errors of 7.60 and 16.07 mm on DROID and RoboLab and adapts to a new embodiment with only ten demonstrations. The generator achieves 69.19% mean success on RoboTwin and outperforms well-established policy models on two real-world tasks, while joint training on source and augmented demonstrations improves target-robot success by 41.5% over augmented-only training.
items.title_zh: TCP4D：面向机器人操作的统一工具中心点跟踪与生成模型
items.summary: TCP4D uses a shared 4D scene representation to both track observed tool-center-point motion and generate future TCP trajectories from monocular video, recovering metric TCP poses and gripper states plus scene geometry and camera parameters, with a cross-embodiment augmentation pipeline.

items.title: Hardware Acceleration of Vision-Language-Action Models with Weight Precision Rising over the Flow Steps
items.raw_content:
Authors: Robin Geens, Simon Haepers, Jonas Crols, Chao Fang, Marian Verhelst

Vision-language-action (VLA) models such as GR00T control robots through an action head: a diffusion transformer that turns noise into a chunk of actions in a few flow-matching steps. Every step re-reads all of the head's weights from DRAM but applies each weight to only about fifty tokens. Inference is therefore memory-bound, and its latency and energy are largely determined by the total number of transferred weight bits. We show that later flow steps attenuate the quantization errors of earlier steps, so the weight precision of an action head should rise over the steps. With plain per-channel rounding and without calibration or training, widths rising over the steps from 2 to 4 bits preserve the closed-loop success of robot policies. These widths transfer 25% fewer bits than 4-bit weights at every step. However, we show that on Jetson AGX Thor, current GPU kernels cannot exploit this per-step precision due to fixed overheads. We therefore present a programmable accelerator whose latency and energy both scale with the transferred weight bits. It decodes entropy-coded weights for bit-serial sub-arrays at the DRAM rate. Because the width changes per step, a run-time allocator divides these sub-arrays between the linear layers and the attention to balance their workloads. The same sub-arrays are thus capable of running action heads of different families and sizes, as well as a vision-language model. On the DRAM side, a requantizer and an entropy encoder at each bank let one stored 8-bit copy replace the copies of all widths. Simulated with LPDDR5X timing, our RTL implementation runs the GR00T N1.6 action head in 8.02 ms per inference with 2, 3, 3 and 4 bits in its four flow steps. With a copy per width and 50% of Thor's memory bandwidth, the accelerator runs this schedule 1.7x faster than Thor in NVFP4, at 9.1x less energy and equal closed-loop success.
items.title_zh: VLA 模型硬件加速：权重精度随流步骤上升
items.summary: The paper shows that later flow-matching steps attenuate earlier quantization errors, so a VLA action head's weight precision can rise over steps; widths rising from 2 to 4 bits preserve closed-loop robot policy success while transferring 25% fewer bits than 4-bit weights at every step, though current Jetson AGX Thor GPU kernels cannot exploit the per-step precision.

items.title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
items.raw_content:
Authors: Junjie Ye, Yiqi Zhao, Muchen Xu, Celina Shiyu Wang, Hao Dong et al.

We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human video and robot trajectories, $Z$-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.
items.title_zh: Z-sight：统一视觉-语言-动作与潜在世界模型
items.summary: Z-sight couples a VLA with generative latent world modeling, predicting the future directly in the visual token space its VLM perceives rather than reconstructing pixels; a foresight expert and continuous action expert are combined with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, achieving 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points).

items.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
items.raw_content:
Authors: Yuseon Choi, Sanghyeon Park, Eunjong Lee, Hanseo Lee, Sangjin Kim

Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. However, realizing this opportunity requires scaling experience banks, introducing substantial storage and search overhead that challenges the capacity, bandwidth, and power constraints of edge systems.
  We propose FlashX, a CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA)-based NAND flash architecture for scalable experience reuse in embodied agents. FlashX exploits CBA's high internal bandwidth for parallel pSLC key search, employing interleaved Compute-in-Flash (CIF) engines to sustain sensing throughput while retaining dense TLC latent storage. Proprioception-aware clustering further reduces search overhead and enables incremental experience acquisition without global reclustering. Evaluations across VLA and WAM workloads demonstrate up to 12.24\%p and 7.43\%p improvements in task success under dense and compute-efficient configurations, respectively. FlashX achieves 2.57$\times$ higher search throughput than the strongest prior NAND search architecture under pSLC sensing, with a further 9.7$\times$ search reduction through clustering. This delivers 1.29--3.95$\times$ end-to-end speedup and 1.12--2.34$\times$ energy efficiency improvement over SSD-based retrieval.
items.title_zh: FlashX：用 CBA NAND 闪存扩展具身智能体经验复用
items.summary: FlashX uses CBA-based NAND flash to scale experience reuse for embodied agents, improving task success by up to 12.24 points and delivering 2.57x higher search throughput.

items.title: Verified Netlist-to-RTL Recovery with LLM Agents
items.raw_content:
Authors: Ahmet Efe, Recep Bugra Uludag, Ulya R. Karpuzcu

Gate-level netlists circulate among IP integrators and foundries and can be extracted from chips. Reverse engineering them into readable register-transfer-level (RTL) code would help an adversary understand and modify a design, but remains difficult because word-level operations are scattered across many gates. Large language models (LLMs) can write and optimize RTL, but often fail to recover it from a whole netlist. We propose LOCA (LOgic Cone Attack), an LLM-based attack that divides an anonymized netlist into logic cones, has parallel agents rewrite them, and assembles compact RTL. Each cone contains the complete next-state logic of a group of related registers, giving an agent a small, meaningful task. Of five partitioning methods tested, only grouped cones lead to recovery. LOCA keeps only RTL proven equivalent to the netlist and measures its quality by compression. Function-preserving obfuscation does not stop LOCA on the tested designs, whereas unknown keys or hidden cell functions prevent it from proving recovery of the original design. Across 21 model-design pairs, LOCA recovers 17, versus 6 with whole-netlist prompting. Per-run recovery across models rises from 5% to 74%, at a median cost below one dollar with a low-cost model.
items.title_zh: LOCA：用 LLM 智能体从网表恢复 RTL
items.summary: LOCA uses parallel LLM agents to recover readable RTL from anonymized gate-level netlists; it recovered 17 of 21 model-design pairs versus 6 with whole-netlist prompting, at a median cost below $1.

items.title: Splice-Core: Low-Order-Bit-Splicing GEMM for Highly Energy-Efficient AI Inference Accelerators
items.raw_content:
Authors: Prabhu Vellaisamy, Hsien-Fu Hung, Andrew Kim, Shawn Blanton, John Paul Shen

Splice-Core is a temporal-unary/binary (tub) hybrid general matrix multiplication (GEMM) unit that minimizes low-order accumulation latency, while retaining value-dependent execution for high-order activation bits. We present two novel processing element (PE) variants: (i) Splice-BP utilizing bit planes, and (ii) Splice-LUT, which selects a shared weight multiple in a single cycle. Compared to a binary systolic array, Splice-BP/Splice-LUT achieve 77.4%/76.4% geometric-mean tile energy reductions, respectively, across 26 INT4 convolutional neural network (CNN) and large language model (LLM) workloads in 45nm. Splice-LUT further increases geometric-mean tile throughput by 44.4% and reduces geometric-mean energy-delay product (EDP) by 6.13x across the 26 configurations. Across the evaluated W8A8 convolution and expert-projection workloads, Splice-BP and Splice-LUT reduce tile energy by 77.3-88.1%. Post-place-and-route INT4 yields 14%/9% smaller area for Splice-BP/Splice-LUT, compared to the systolic array.
items.title_zh: Splice-Core：低位拼接 GEMM 节能 AI 加速器
items.summary: Splice-Core is a hybrid temporal-unary/binary GEMM unit for AI inference; its Splice-BP and Splice-LUT variants cut tile energy by about 77% and Splice-LUT improves energy-delay product by 6.13x across 26 INT4 workloads.

items.title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience
items.raw_content:
Authors: EngineAI

A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. Existing egocentric video datasets cover many of these activities but provide little synchronized whole-body motion data for learning loco-manipulation at scale. We build Awaken-Human, which pairs approximately 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion and covers more than 100 skills. Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert. We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and $π_{0.5}$ in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.
items.title_zh: Awaken-HI：用全身人类经验扩展人形机器人智能
items.summary: EngineAI built Awaken-Human, about 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body motion, and trained Awaken-HI, which reaches 93.75% mean success across eight tasks and beats GR00T N1.7 and π0.5.

items.title: 3D-NAND-CIM: A Hybrid-Bonded 3D-NAND-Flash-based Analog In-Memory-Compute macro offering 4.8M weights/mm$^2$
items.raw_content:
Authors: Pritish Narayanan, Athanasios Vasilopoulos, Geoffrey W. Burr, Manuel Le Gallo, Bill Filipiak et al.

We describe an analog-in-memory-compute macro hybrid-bonding a 14nm logic die onto a 3D NAND Flash memory wafer, achieving weight density of 4.8M weights/mm$^2$. Weights are programmed to 1-of-16 conductances. MACs with current-controlled oscillator ADCs show weight-equivalent precision between 3 and 4 bits for 8-bit inputs on multiple NAND tiers at energy efficiencies up to 4.2 TOPS/W. A charge-retention circuit improves accuracy, with $\sim$0.4% (3.23%) accuracy drop on a WideResNet for CIFAR-10 (100).
items.title_zh: 3D-NAND-CIM：混合键合 3D NAND 模拟存内计算宏，密度达 480 万权重/mm²
items.summary: The work describes an analog in-memory-compute macro that hybrid-bonds a 14nm logic die onto a 3D NAND Flash wafer, reaching 4.8 million weights per square millimeter, 3-4 bit weight-equivalent precision for 8-bit inputs and energy efficiency up to 4.2 TOPS/W, with a charge-retention circuit limiting accuracy loss on WideResNet.

items.title: Selective ROM Weight Storage for Responsive LLM Control on Edge Robots
items.raw_content:
Authors: Boxiang Song, Zhihong Chen, Xiaoyu Hao, Jinhong Huang, Chengkai Zhu et al.

Edge robots increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for complex tasks, demanding efficient inference alongside timely control. Limited memory capacity constrains model deployment, while repeated weight transfers during decoding compete with activations and KV cache for external bandwidth. Sequential generation of robot actions further delays decisions and periodic control on shared hardware. We present a hybrid memory architecture with heterogeneous scheduling to address these bottlenecks jointly. Banked ROM stores selected fixed weights and supplies a standard compute array through a dedicated datapath. LPDDR retains the remaining weights and mutable state, preserving model flexibility. Coordinated operand delivery and preemption at output slice boundaries accelerate inference while limiting interference with periodic control. A structured decision interface scores candidate phases in a single forward pass, avoiding sequential token generation for routine choices. Together, these mechanisms improve memory service, compute access, and decision execution for edge robotic workloads. Experiments with Qwen3-8B achieve a peak decode speedup of 1.56$\times$ and reduce P99 task response time by a factor of approximately 227.27$\times$, while completing 100.00\% of the tested grasping and transport tasks.
items.title_zh: 面向边缘机器人响应的选择性 ROM 权重存储
items.summary: The paper presents a hybrid memory architecture that stores selected fixed LLM weights in banked ROM with a dedicated datapath while keeping remaining weights and mutable state in LPDDR, plus a structured decision interface that scores candidate phases in one forward pass; experiments with Qwen3-8B reach a 1.56x peak decode speedup and cut P99 task response time by about 227x while completing all tested grasping and transport tasks.

items.title: Weight-Space Backdoors in Open-Weight LLMs: Cross-Architecture Attacks and Blind Model Forensics
items.raw_content:
Authors: Mohammed Tanveer

Open-weight language models are vulnerable to trigger-conditioned behaviors introduced through sparse post-training weight modifications, creating supply-chain risks beyond conventional provenance checks. We present Neural Sentinel, a cross-architecture study of gradient-guided backdoor insertion and model forensics spanning 18 checkpoints across 14 architecture families (124M-31.3B parameters), including state-space and recurrent models.
  On Phi-2, modifying approximately 0.0002% of parameters induced an exact short-marker output after 300 steps (332 seconds), with mean next-token KL divergence of $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$ and 100% top-1 agreement over evaluated positions of eight fixed reference prompts. Separate experiments produced structured tool-call-formatted outputs without establishing downstream execution. We identify three procedure-dependent response regimes -- Gradient-Permeable, Scale-Threshold, and Gradient-Fragmented -- and evaluate PPO-based weight-space exploration, which showed no statistically significant advantage over random search.
  For defense, Neural Sentinel combines weight-difference analysis, trigger discovery, activation probing, and contextual output inspection. In a 22-artifact development cohort, its reference-optional scanner classified 4/5 backdoored artifacts as BACKDOORED; the remaining positive and all 17 clean artifacts were SUSPICIOUS. These findings establish the feasibility of sparse conditional-output insertion and evidence-producing forensic triage, while identifying limitations in behavioral-drift assessment and clean-model admission.
items.title_zh: 开源权重 LLM 的权重空间后门：跨架构攻击与盲测模型取证
items.summary: Neural Sentinel studies gradient-guided backdoor insertion and model forensics across 18 checkpoints from 14 architecture families; on Phi-2, modifying about 0.0002% of parameters induced an exact short-marker output after 300 steps with tiny KL divergence and 100% top-1 agreement on eight reference prompts, and its scanner classified 4 of 5 backdoored artifacts as backdoored while marking all 17 clean artifacts suspicious.

items.title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
items.raw_content:
Authors: Xu Lin, Ruilin Yao, Haoran Xu, Zixiang Wang, Ming Ma et al.

Vision Banana showed that a closed image generator, instruction-tuned to paint perception outputs as RGB images, becomes a generalist vision model. Does this carry over to \emph{open} generators, and if not, what fails? We answer with \textbf{Open Vision Banana (OVB)}, an open framework that adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into one instruction-driven model for metric depth, semantic, instance, and referring segmentation, using a single shared low-rank adapter and public data. Each task is a \emph{task contract} whose RGB encoder, instruction, and decoder share one specification and are checked before training. Studying 42 externally evaluated checkpoints from two 100k-update runs, six exact weight-space merges, and eight controlled shorter runs, we find that the gap to the closed system is specific and measurable. Geometry is learned early while absolute scale is not: median-aligned NYUv2 $δ_1$ stays at 0.89--0.93 throughout training as unaligned $δ_1$ wanders between 0.11 and 0.50. The scale is not committed by a single sample: a ten-seed ensemble lifts unaligned $δ_1$ from 0.348 to 0.516 without retraining. Depth and 2D segmentation compete for the shared adapter, and weight merging moves along this trade-off without escaping it. Finally, lower validation flow loss comes with lower Cityscapes accuracy (Spearman $ρ\approx-0.9$ between loss reduction and mIoU), so the loss cannot select checkpoints. We release code, contracts, training data, and all evaluation outputs.
items.title_zh: Open Vision Banana：在 RGB 空间通过生成实现统一视觉感知的开源框架
items.summary: Open Vision Banana adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into one instruction-driven model for metric depth, semantic, instance and referring segmentation with a single shared low-rank adapter and public data; the study finds geometry is learned early but absolute scale is not, and that depth and 2D segmentation compete for the shared adapter, with code, contracts, training data and evaluation outputs released.
